speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. Agent; you've mentioned experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To start, is your dizziness a sensation of the room spinning around you (vertigo), or does it feel like you are fainting or unsteady on your feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; you describe constant vertigo rather than presyncope. Did the onset of these spinning sensations happen suddenly and reach its peak intensity within seconds, or did it develop gradually over a period of minutes?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The VNG results are normal, which is interesting given your bilateral hearing loss and constant vertigo. Since the recent garlic intake and lack of response to antihistamines don't fit a typical viral labyrinthitis picture, do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or recent upper respiratory infections besides the cold?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal Video Head Impulse Test (VNG) results are puzzling given your constant vertigo and bilateral hearing loss. Could you describe exactly how the garlic intake was prepared or if you experienced any skin rash or joint pain recently?
